learning_outcomes.text: Students master the fundamentals of one-dimensional analysis. They can confidently work with limits, functions, power series, and integrals. They understand central concepts such as continuity, differentiability, or integrability, and are familiar with important statements regarding these. Students can comprehend the justifications for these statements presented in the lecture and independently justify simple statements based on them.
Students master the fundamentals of vector space theory. They can effortlessly use vectors, linear mappings, and matrices.
They have fundamental knowledge of Fourier series.

Furthermore, students master the theoretical and practical handling of initial value problems for ordinary differential equations. They can apply classical solution methods for linear differential equations.

Students master differential calculus for vector-valued functions of several variables and techniques of vector analysis, such as the definition and application of differential operators, the calculation of domain, curve, and surface integrals, and central integral theorems.
They have fundamental knowledge of partial differential equations and master basic concepts of stochastics.

syllabus_topics: Differential calculus of one real variable

assessment_methods.method: Study achievement (Übungsscheine) for Higher Mathematics I
Study achievement (Übungsscheine) for Higher Mathematics II
Study achievement (Übungsscheine) for Higher Mathematics III

assessment_rules: The assessment consists of three written partial exams, each 120 minutes in duration, and three study achievements (Übungsscheine). Passing an Übungsschein in Higher Mathematics I, II, or III is a prerequisite for participating in the corresponding written exam.
